reason: '2-bracteolate' on the pedicels means bracteoles are present (the flora goes on 'bracteoles linear'). The count of 2 and the mid-pedicel position could be added as a count annotation, but presence is true.
Seeds 100-150 per capsule: a count of 100-150 is right.
Corolla funnelform, 5-6 mm: in FOC a single bare measurement of the corolla is its length.

fix: 'Sheathing leaves' that cover an orchid pseudobulb are cataphylls (scale leaves), not leaves in general. Map 'sheathing leaves' to scale leaf (or keep the modifier) so that it is not merged with the foliage leaves.
reason: Only the sheathing leaves become fibrous with age. The foliage leaves are said to be membranous, so 'leaf fibrous when old' contradicts the flora for the foliage leaves.
The seeds are glabrous when mature, and the stage slot 'mature' is set.
'gynophore ± long' gives the gynophore as rather long, and the 'approximately' qualifier is kept. In a genus description this can also mean 'of varying length', so the reading is weak.
Inflorescences subcapitate, read as approximately capitate. The 'in ours' restriction applies to the whole genus treatment.
'caruncle absent' on the seed: negated presence of caruncle is right.
Lower and middle stem leaves are ± sessile. The position slot (lower/middle cauline) is missing, but nothing says the other leaves are petiolate, so the statement is not made false.

fix: 'not strongly X' negates the degree, not the presence: 'not strongly veined' = veins faint or not prominent, never 'veins absent'. Add 'not strongly'/'not conspicuously' to the degree-negation patterns.
reason: The leaflets have veins (the midrib is even named as an exception). The flora says they are not prominent, not that the vascular bundles are absent.
Lamina coriaceous.
Inner phyllaries 2.5-3 × 0.2-0.4 cm: the width of 0.2-0.4 cm is right, and the 'inner' context is set.
The ovary is adnate to the disk (floral disc FLOPO_0986025). 'Lower part' only limits the extent of the fusion.

fix: A position word in the subject noun phrase ('uppermost leaves', 'lower leaves') must fill the position slot whenever an absence is annotated. Without it, the absence is claimed for every leaf.
reason: Only the uppermost cauline leaves lack a blade. The basal leaves are described with lobed blades, so 'leaf lamina absent' is false without the position.
Calyx lobes (sepal) with the apex ± acute or obtuse. Both values are apex shapes, given as alternatives.
Leaf blade adaxially pubescent: the bearer is replaced by the adaxial epidermis.
The capsule apex is pubescent (with gland-tipped hairs). The part restriction to the apex is set. That the hairs are glandular is not recorded, but nothing stated is false.
Stamens usually 3, with the frequency 'usually'. The male-flower context is implicit from 'Male spikes'.
Often 1-2 small empty bracts along the male peduncles: the count of 1-2 with 'often' is right. The peduncle is the whole that carries them.
Branchlets brownish, read as approximately brown.
Involucres obconic to campanulate: a shape continuum from obconical to campanulate.
Petiole 1-1.5 cm long.
Stem 25-60 cm tall: a height of 25-60 cm is right.
Fruit more or less tuberculate.
The hairs of the petiole indumentum are more or less spreading. A whole slot (petiole) would be better, but trichome spreading is true as stated.

fix: 'Fruit mûr ...' / 'ripe fruit ...': the adjective 'mûr' after the noun must fill the stage slot, the same way 'when mature' does.
reason: The flora gives the colour of the ripe fruit only ('Fruit mûr rouge vif ou rose clair'). Unripe fruits are not that colour, so the colour without the stage is false for young fruit.

fix: 'à la face inférieure/supérieure' after a qualitative relation must set the bearer scope (substituted bearer abaxial/adaxial epidermis), as 'abaxially' does in English.
reason: Only the lower face is pubescent then glabrescent. The upper face is said to be glabrous even when young, so the annotation on the whole lamina contradicts the flora.
Leaf blade apex acuminate, with the bearer replaced by the leaf lamina tip.
Stipules shortly adnate to the petiole.

fix: 'X not seen', 'X unknown' and 'X not known' are statements about the material studied, not about absence. Exclude them from the negation pattern and emit no annotation.
reason: 'Flowers not seen' means the author had no flowering material. It does not say the plant lacks flowers.
